When we choose to love Allah passionately, when we choose to become obsessed about Him, when we are completely devoted and loyal to Him, when we completely trust Him and lean upon Him, When we're totally impressed and amazed by His loftiness, His greatness, His magnificence, when we know that we can always unconditionally turn to Him for protection and refuge, then the natural outcome of the sum of all of these love-based emotions is obedience. But what happens when you pass that light through a prism? We know that prism is just a medium. It's a medium of glass, right? And when this white light, it hits this glass, it refracts, right? It bends. And the result of that, a whole spectrum of colors show up from violet to red and everything in between. In the same way when the light of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala hits creation, you know, because the Quran tells us that Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth, right?

He is the light of the heavens and the earth. So what happens is that when this pure light of Allah's essence, when it hits creation, when it enters the realm of physicality, it refracts into the spectrum of these divine attributes. You see? This is why we get all these different manifestations of Allah's essence in this universe. So this Alam, you know, you can look at it as a prism that is manifesting Allah's various attributes in creations for us to observe.

So, in one instance, we see that Allah is Kareem, right? We see that He is generous. So, in another instance, the universe shows us that Allah is Jabbar, He is the compeller. In another instance, the aalam reveals to us that He is Qahar, the subduer. In another instance, we see that He is Aziz, the powerful. In another instance, we see that He is Muzil, the humiliator. In another we see that he is Mawiz, the bestower of honor.

So the Aalam essentially serves as this colossal theater for the divine manifestations of these attributes of Allah. And that is how we come to know about him. Now why did he set the stage up in this way? Because like I mentioned earlier, the human intellect It learns by defining and limiting things. Right? Just as the body works by breaking down food. So if you look at how the intellect works, it works just like the body.

In order to digest knowledge, it has to take in the whole, break it down into parts, and then understand each part individually. Right? Only then it can sum those parts up again to understand the whole. So the Aalam it presents us these parts in the form of these divine attributes so that we can reflect on them individually and then sum them up to put together a more complete understanding of our Creator.

So this is the essential theme of Quran. It invites us to reflect on the heavens and the earth, the horizons and the soul Because through that very reflection, we can recognize our creator and his abilities. And then once we've done that, it turns our attention inward onto the soul, the nafs, to understand the purpose of our creation. Right? So now what is the purpose of our creation?

Scholars say that there are three reasons for the creation of human beings and what's beautiful about this distinction is that it allows for purposeful existence for not just Muslims but for people of other beliefs as well or even people without belief. So he says that the first reason for creation of human beings he says is Imara. Right? Cultivation. Allah says, We brought you forth from the earth to cultivate it.

That's the first reason. The second reason, He says, is ibada. We only created the jinn which are beings of the unseen realm and humans which are beings of the seen realm for the purpose of ibada. for willing worship. So Ibn Abbas said in a narration that the purpose behind the creation of human beings was also li'arifun Allah to know Allah and to know Allah is to love Allah.

So those of you who have heard my session on those on that stages of love you know that Ubudiyya is one of the levels of muhabbah right? is one of the higher levels of love. Therefore he created the Jinn and the human beings to love him. Right? So... ... it can also be taken as I did not create Jinn and man except to love me. So those are the two reasons.

The third and the last reason for creation of human being he says is Khilafa. We made you Khulafa because the Khalifa, the Caliph is the one who stands in place of somebody else right? He is the one who is left behind. He is left behind to stand in the place of someone else. In other words, a Khalifa is a steward. Allah created us as His stewards on this earth.

Why? So that He can witness what we do with all the external and internal gifts that He blessed us with. That's the test. Now, there are two types of Khilafah. There are two types of Khulafa. We have been made a Caliph over ourselves and then over others. So for the Khilafa of the Self, Allah says, He said to the angels, I have decided to create a Caliph in this earth.

And then in Surah Swad, He says, He says, O Daud, we have made you a caliph in the earth. So this is the second type of Khilafa that is mentioned in the Quran. So there are two types of Khilafa. The first is to rule yourself and the second is to rule others. but the condition of ruling others is that you rule yourself first, that you take control and mastery of your nafs first and so here in this verse Tawud is being told we have put you in the earth to rule over others because he was made a ruler over Bani Israel, right?

So, so that you can judge among them with the truth and then he says do not follow your own caprice do not follow your own whims in other words you have to rule yourself first before you can rule others you see because if you do not do that and the fa in the you see begins with fa the fa here is for causation Because if you do not do that, if you do follow your caprice, if you do follow your whims, your appetites, then it will lead you astray from the path of Allah.

So what are we as caliphs of Allah and how are we doing as Allah's representatives on earth? So, I'd like to spend a little time talking about this today because I think it's really important to put this into perspective. How are we doing as Allah's representatives? He says, We will show them our signs in the horizon and in our own souls. Allah will let us know through the signs of what we see around us.

He will let us know the reality of our existence. So let's look at some of the signs that we see in the horizons today. Right? Let's reflect on some of these signs to understand who we are and how we are doing as caliphs of Allah. Just as a physician would look at the symptoms of a sick patient. So Allah says in Surah Room He says, Zahar al-fasadu fil barri wal bahari bima kasabad aydi an naas liyudhika hum wa adal ladi amilu la'allahum yarji'um He says, Zahar al-fasadu fil barri wal bahari bima kasabad aydi an naas Mischief, corruption, pollution has appeared on the land and sea because of what the hands of men have earned.

And again the lamb here is for causation. So that Allah can give them a taste of their deeds in order for them to turn back to Him. So we see that the reason Allah makes our negative actions have negative repercussions is in order for us to return back to Allah. This is why negative actions have negative consequences so that, you know, it helps us return back to Allah.

Scholars say that Zahar al-Fasad is actually a nuqs filbahri walbahr. So it means the diminished blessings of Allah on earth. You lose the blessings of the earth. And it also means Al-Qahat which is droughts and famines and you know all the other harm that comes in agriculture. the fruit of the land you know the land stops growing crops it also means that the benefits of the oceans disappear from the fish and the other animals that live in the oceans you know like the whales and all of this is going to happen because of what we earn from our own sinfulness because human beings even though created in the best of forms in the very image of its creator you know with all of his divine attributes, that human being is still capable of extreme corruption when he deviates from his divinity, when he deviates from his original state.

This is that very concern that the angels expressed when Allah mentioned the creation of Adam. He said, This is what the angel said, right? Are you seriously considering creating a species in this earth who will create facade and who will spill blood? The word facade if you look at it in the English dictionary it means rottenness, spoilness, corruption, decay, decomposition, putrid, depravity, wickedness, viciousness, iniquity, immorality, weakness, Perversion, wrongness, incorrectness, all of these are meanings embodied in the word facade.

If you look at the word pollution in the English dictionary, it says, undesirable state of the natural environment being contaminated with harmful substances as consequences of human activities. You see, this is the result. So even in our language, pollution is a dominant problem on the planet. You know, we as human beings, we are responsible for the present state of the earth today. Our conditions of hardships in the form of famines and extreme weathers and earthquakes and floods, these are nothing more than Bima Kathabat Aidi and nass from what our own hands have earned.

Many countries are in a major crisis because of fires that were started in forests, right? Climate changes are driving up temperatures. And as these temperatures rise, there are more incidents of fire. Another aspect of this facade is the air itself. In India, it has been estimated that half a million people die from air pollution, half a million people. We had 15,000 people die from terrorism and the US government had moved heavens and earth to have this war on terrorism.

Yet half a million people suffer and die from air pollution just in India. Where's the war against that? Where's the war against noise pollution? In Pakistan and India, look at the levels of noise pollution in the form of honking and yelling and screaming and the noise from rickshaws and taxis, you know, broken silencers. That's all man-made facade. Today we know that the world is rapidly moving towards desertification, right?

This is because what we're losing what they call topsoil. Desertification is literally where a place that once had foliage it turns into desert and it has already happened in large portions of fertile land and this problem just continues to grow. I was reading this book the other day in which it said that there was once a time when all of North Africa was so fertile you know that before Banu Hilau, before they got into Africa, he wrote that a squirrel could run from Sinjab, from Egypt all the way to Morocco without its feet ever touching the ground.

Imagine that. A squirrel could run from Egypt to Morocco without its feet ever touching the ground. The land was so fertile but when these Banu Hilau, when they entered North Africa they were like locusts. They devoured all the resources. So, desertification is another example of ... from what our own hands have earned. Another aspect of Fasad, as Allah says, you know, in the Quran, The earth has been put out for the Anam.

The word Anam comes from naum, which means sleep. So Anam are creatures that sleep. So this verse is actually talking about all sentient beings. It is not just about human beings. So it includes the animal kingdom. Allah says in the Quran, That there is no creature on the earth that walks the earth. And there is no bird that flies with its two wings, except that they have communities like unto you.

Allah tells us that the animal kingdoms are communities just like us. And then He says, That He did not leave anything out from this book. Even the animals are acknowledged in the Quran. We know that there are animals that mate for life. We know that animals make huge pilgrimage and you know and vast migrations to places just like we do. Right? And today because of the sins of mankind, you know animals have all these problems.

I mean dogs are on Prozac. In the United States, they put dogs on Prozac, which are antidepressants because they are depressed in the houses of depressed and miserable people. Dogs are not naturally depressed animals, but there are so many houses in the US that are so sick that the dogs and the cats themselves get sick because they are sentient beings, they are emotional creatures. They feel and experience emotions just like we do.

So there are all these examples of facade that we see in the horizons. Look at the problem of endangered species caused by the hands of man. There are like, I think there are 25 critically endangered species of the world that are from the most beautiful and the most majestic animals. Think about that. These are animals that the ancient Arabs used to name their children after. Animals like, you know, lions and tigers, Asad and Fahad.

Right? These are animals that the Arabs, they named their men after. They used to name them after these Muftarisad, you know, after animals that attacked their prey. that they would name the men after these muftarisat, these animals that attack the prey. And then they would name their women after the prey itself, you know, like Maha and Ghazala. You know, so Fahad goes after Maha and she doesn't stand a chance.

So that was the ancient Arab concept, right? You know, that is why we have all these beautiful names in Arabic. But what's interesting is that if you look at the species that are endangered today, they're not the cockroaches, they're not the rats, they're not the snakes, they're flourishing. The animals and species that are endangered are the ones that represent the divine qualities within us that are disappearing right the eagle the peregrine the lion the tiger the elephants these are the animals that represent those great qualities in human beings that are disappearing today within your own souls why don't you reflect We've got plenty of cockroaches out there in human disguise.

We've got plenty of rats and snakes out there in human disguise, taking hold of the greatest offices in countries, becoming presidents and things like that. But what we do not find is the courage of lions. What we do not find today is the majesty of the eagles in human form. These are qualities that are extinct from human beings today. And I can go on and on and I'm sure you can think of and add so much more.

But this is what we're doing as caliphs and the stewards of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. We are destroying the very earth that sustains us and provides us with our livelihood. And then we complain that we have problems. You know why doesn't Allah solve all our problems? Why should He? He's not our janitor, He's not our servant, He's not our errand boy. No, He created us in His image so that we could create Jannah on earth, just as He created Jannah on heaven.

Why else do you think Adam alaihis salam was created in Jannah? Just for fun? If He was created for the earth, I am planning to create a caliph on Earth why why did he need to be created in Jannah when he was being created for Earth he could have been directly created in on the Earth right then why did Allah create him in Jannah he was created in Jannah so that he could see and experience the beauty of that place so that when he comes to the Earth He could cultivate that land and create that same Jannah on earth.

That is the purpose of a caliph, of a Khalifa. He brought you forth from the earth in order to cultivate it, in order to create the same Jannah on this earth. And what did we do? And why did this happen? You know, how did things get so bad and so out of hand? because of our corruption, because of our facade, our deviation from the divine attributes and the majestic qualities that Allah created us with.

And so this is why he created the Aalameen for us so that we can study the signs of the horizons, the heavens and the earth to learn the ideal conditions of the Nafs. the ideal condition of the soul through his divine attributes. But we as human beings, as Khalifatullah, we have failed miserably and we have proven that the angels did have valid grounds for their concerns. That's what we have proved, that they clearly knew what they were talking about when they said, Do you really wish to create someone on this earth who will sow corruption and spill blood?

Obviously, they knew what they were talking about. So what is it that we have deviated from? We have deviated from the divine attributes. We have deviated from the character of Allah. The word for character in Arabic is Akhlaq, right? And the word Akhlaq comes from the word Khulq. Akhlaq is the plural, Khulq is the singular. And this is really interesting because we are called Khalq, right? The word Khalq means creation.

Sadaf, your mic is on. Can you please turn it off? No problem. Right? So hulk means character and hulk means creation, which is related to the body. Right? So hulk is related to the body. and the body exists in the horizons and Khulk which means character it belongs to the soul, it belongs to the nafs and they're both made-up of the same letters and in the same sequence.

So according to the science of Arabic both these words are closely related in meaning. The word Khalq is related to the body which is nourished by this physical world, the word Khulk Character, it takes its nourishment from the spiritual world. You see? Khalq represents the existence of the body. Khulq represents the existence of the soul. And both these words, they begin with the letter Kha which is a sound of friction in Arabic, right?

Kha and friction takes effort. So Kha in Arabic is a sound of effort. This is because the body takes effort to develop and so does character. Character takes a lot of effort to develop. Therefore, if Khalq is the essence of the body then Khulq or character is the essence of the soul. When we die, the body returns back into the earth with whatever it has acquired from the physical world and the soul returns back to the spiritual world with its nourishment of character that it has developed in this world.

That's our true earning. That's our character is our true accomplishment. That's our real acquisition. Khulk character. A soul that returns back to its master without a developed Khulk is an impoverished soul. It is the soul that has failed to fulfill its purpose of khilpa it has failed the purpose of its creation and that's why a weak soul cannot enter Jannah because when the body is weak it cannot benefit from the offerings of this physical world right?

I mean we know that this world has a lot to offer in terms of temporal pleasures but if you're extremely weak if you can't even get off your bed you're not going to be able to enjoy those pleasures right? In the same way a soul that is empty, that is bankrupt of Akhlaq is not going to be able to benefit from the pleasures of the afterlife. It's as simple as that.

Now how is character developed? It is developed through revelation. As I said Quran is an You know if you look at it in an oversimplified statement, Quran is the explanation of divine attributes of Allah. It explains the attributes of Allah and why he has those attributes. Right? He is Azim because he created this massive universe. The size of this universe tells us that he's Azim. He is Qawi.

He's all-powerful. Because not only did He create this massive universe, He created it with a single command qun be and fayakun it was. So in essence, Quran is just the description of Allah's attributes explaining why He is al-ilah. He created all of us as ilah but then gave us through the aalam, He gave us these signs for us to recognize that He is the al-ilah, He is Allah.

Our hearts witness these divine attributes in the light of revelation which then creates belief, iman. The more the heart understands revelation the more we grow in our belief which then nourishes and develops our character. And so character is nothing more than absorbing these divine attributes into the heart from revelation and then reflecting those same divine attributes into the rest of Allah's creation. That is what character is.

It is internalizing, developing, and training the heart in the light of these divine attributes. And then reflecting them in our interactions with Allah's creation. That is Aflaq. And that is Islam. Islam is all about interactions. It is all about Muhammad. Now, there are three types of interactions in Islam. There is the interaction with Allah , the rights of Allah. There is interacting with the self which is or the right of the soul.

And then interaction with the creations of Allah which is , the rights of others, the right of other slaves. So, I'll just quickly talk about each of these so that you see how these are all related to the attributes of Allah. So, the first is the right of Allah. Right? What right does Allah have over us? That we recognize His attributes in the heavens and the earth and we approach Him with love for everything that He has done for us.

And then out of that love we willingly obey and serve Him as faithful slaves which is Rubudiya. So, it is the right of the Rabb that we become Aabd. That we worship Him recognizing the fact that only He deserves to be worshipped. That is the right of the Creator over His creation. Right? Now, what is the right of the self? The right of the self is to reflect on the attributes of Allah in the Aalam through the teachings of Quran, to learn those attributes, those qualities, basically to learn the character of our master and to then internalize and harvest those qualities within our own hearts to develop our own character, our own Akhlaq.

Because we have been created in imamate of our master. We have been created to represent our master on this earth which means we have to adopt the qualities and characteristics of our master. Right? That is what a Khalifa is, a representative. You can't represent unless you become like the one you are representing. Right? So, the second step of Haqqun Nafs is that you train it in the attributes of Allah, in the character of Allah.

So, for instance, Allah is qareem. He is generous. Therefore, it is the right of my soul that I train it to be generous. Generous with who? Generous with myself. What is the greatest generosity that I can show myself? To try to protect it from sins and put it to work in good deeds. That is the greatest generosity for my soul. We know that Allah is al-haqq He is truthful.

So it is the right of my soul that I train it to be truthful. With who? With myself. What is the greatest falsehood that the nafs is trapped in? The greatest lie that the nafs is trapped in is the delusion of this reality of dunya. So I must train myself on a daily basis to try to wake up from my delusions about this world. Right? I need to wake up to the reality that I'm only here for a short period of time.

Everything that I'm working for in the worldly sense will be left behind. I will be left with nothing other than this title of Mayyat. You know, my loved ones, the people that I am slaving for day and night, they will be the first to dump me in a grave and throw dirt in my face. So I better not sacrifice my afterlife for this temporary life, you know, by eating haram, by So that's being truthful to the self.

So the right of the self is that I internalize the attributes of Allah and train myself in those attributes in order to develop my character so that I can realize the potential that I was created with. I was created in imamate of God to act like God and God is nothing other than just. This is why one of the divine names of Allah is Al-Mu'min, which essentially means, you know, the giver of tranquility, the one who brings peace.

You know, Mu'min comes from the word Aman, which means peace. So that is the right of my nafs that I train it in the attributes of Allah. And finally, there is the right of others. Now what are the right of others? So right of Allah was recognizing His divine attributes in creation and submitting to Him willingly out of love in the form of ibada. Right? Right of the self was to internalize those divine attributes.

I've already recognized them. The next step is to internalize those divine attributes to build my own character, to align it with the character of Allah, to become like the creator. Once that character has developed, only then the final rite of Qaqooq al Ibaat comes into play, which is the idea of now reflecting those divine attributes of Allah in interactions with creation. We trained ourselves to become generous with our own self.

Now it's time to reflect that generosity onto others in our dealings with them. We trained ourselves to be truthful and sincere with our own nafs. Now it's time to reflect that truthfulness, that sidq, that sincerity in our dealings with others. We've recognized how Allah is forgiving with us, how He's patient with us. We now have to reflect those attributes by being patient and forgiving with others. And that is not an easy task.

this is why one has to go through the training of fulfilling the previous two rights before he can fulfill this third right and our problem today is that everyone is a preacher you know nobody takes the time to fix themselves but they are when it comes to preaching everybody is a teacher everybody is enforcing things on others I mean I'm not an enforcer I just share knowledge So there's a difference between teaching and between enforcing.

But today, you know, everybody's the first, oh, you're doing that wrong, you should be doing that, that, you know, you're going to hell. That's pretty much, you know, you can't even put a shirt on today without getting some criticism from someone. Cannot even mop the floor without somebody telling you, oh, you have to go clockwise and not anti-clockwise, I mean, right? But people never take the time to actually develop their own character, the person saying that usually doesn't have the most perfect character.

That person is full of flaws himself, but they are enjoying, but they, you know, force that knowledge on others. And that is why it's not working. That is why we have this really big problem in Islam today within our community, within the Suleimani Jamaat, outside of the Suleimani Jamaat where children are developing this hatred for the religion because it's, you know, their first thing is You don't pray five times a day.

Why you keep forcing that prayer on me? So we first have to develop our own self and that's why this is so... because even dealing with people is not easy. You know, a man once came to the Messenger of Allah and he said, O Messenger of Allah, I give him. but he withholds from me. I come to him but he cuts me off. What should I do?

The Prophet said, That is Salatul Rahim. What you're doing is the right thing. Continue meeting him even though he is cutting you off. That is Islam and that's hard work. I mean don't think this is an easy religion. There are many easy religions in this world. Islam is not one of them. Islam demands hard work. it is not easy to become godlike but then we want to be people that strive right we want to be people that honor ourselves that we don't just take a handout from even from Allah we want to earn our rewards because Allah created us as honored creatures right we have ennobled the children of Adam We made you leaders over the land and the oceans.

We gave you a heart. We gave you an intellect. We nourished it through our revelation. We gave you the ability to overcome the worst aspects of yourself. And even if you capitulate from time to time, we've given you the means to renew and restore your soul through Tawbah, through repentance. What a gift from Allah. So this is what we have to do. And we have to do it with Ikhlas, with sincerity.

Only for the sake of Allah. But that's not going to be easy. So these are the three dimensions of Allah. The right of Allah, the right of the self, and the right of others. Recognizing the attributes of Allah in the heavens and the earth help us understand the rights of Allah. Internalizing those divine attributes to develop our character is the right of the soul. It's . Reflecting those divine attributes onto creation of Allah is the right of others.

It is the right... and because this last one is the most challenging of all it cannot be accomplished unless and until the soul has first been illuminated with the character of Allah. This is why RasulAllah said, Adopt the character and the qualities of Allah. You know there's a narration in which RasulAllah once saw a man talking to Mawlana Ali in a very disrespectful manner, right? And in return Mawlana Ali responded back to this guy with complete kindness, complete humility.

But despite his kindness, this man continued to act in a disrespectful manner with him. But Maulana Ali kept responding with kindness over and over and over again. And then finally when the man left, the Prophet asked him, Ya Ali, I saw this man talk to you in such a disrespectful manner. You know, he treated you in such a horrible way over and over again and yet you kept showing him kindness and respect in return.

Why is that? And Maulana Ali said, Ya Rasulullah, If this man is not willing to give up his wretched and evil nature to interact with me, why should I give up my good character to interact with him? Subhanallah, what a beautiful statement. If this man is not willing to give up his wretched and evil nature in his interaction with me, then why should I give up my good character in my interaction with him?

In other words, if this man continues to hold on to something ugly, why should I let go of something beautiful that I possess? That's the beauty of Akhlaq. And this is why we follow the example of Rasulullah who according to the Quran reached the pinnacle of Akhlaq. through his character and nothing other than his character, he purified the most barbaric and the most vile group of people that ever walked this earth.

I mean read the history of Islam. You know understand the mentality of these people he was sent to Rifaam. Just think if you were sent to these people, just put yourself in his shoes. These were the worst, they were worse than animals. There was not a single virtue that existed in them. They were insane. They would eat the flesh of elephants and crocodiles. When they ate a goat, they would even boil and eat its leather.

They would burn their enemies alive in a bonfire. They would rip out their skin and wear it like a scarf while they were alive, the enemy. They would crack open their skull and use it as a cup to drink wine in. Their women would dye their clothes in the blood of their enemies and wear it. They were so barbaric that they would not just kill their enemy, they would tie that enemy's camel to his grave and starve it to death.

That's how barbaric these people were. Sons would marry their mothers. Fathers married their daughters. Daughters were buried alive. They used the children of their enemy for target practice. Even their prayers were barbaric. Can you imagine that? The prayers were horrific. Ya rabbi falataja al-hayati muzillatu wala mawtati bainan nisa'in nawa'ihi walaa kin qateelan tamzaquttairi hawlahu wa tashrubu girbanu dammi min jawaarihi O Lord, do not disgrace me in my life by letting me die on a bed between grieving women.

Give me a death where birds are tearing out my flesh and crows are drinking the fresh blood gushing out of my limbs. I mean, this was their prayers. This was the state of the Arabs when Rasulullah was sent between them. Can you imagine that? This was the group he was sent to reform. And look what he did. Subhanallah. He converted these people into Rahmatullah Alaihi. Today we don't even mention their names without saying Rahmatullah Alaihi after it.

May Allah have mercy on them. That is the kind of character he He cultivated within them. And this is by their own admission, the admission of these own Jahili Arabs on the day of Qadir when Rasulullah asked Am I not more beloved to you than your own souls? What did they say? Indeed you are a Prophet of Allah. We were animals. You turned us into human beings.

And how did he do that? Through his impeccable Akhlaq. By internalizing the divine attributes of his creator, by absorbing them to develop this immaculate character and then finally reflecting those very same attributes into creation with such intensity that the Creator Himself had to acknowledge in the Quran . Indeed, no doubt about it, you have achieved the utmost and the most exalted level of character. SubhanAllah. May Allah grant us a few rays from the light of that sun that shined in the form of Rasulullah . And may Allah, you know, give us the tawfiq to act in some fashion as his khalifa, as his representatives. And the only way that can happen is through this training of adopting the characteristics of Allah. Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen Wassalatu Wassalamu Ala Rasuli Saida Muhammadan Khatimin Nabin Wassalin Waalahi Waasi Alibnabi Talib Al Fateha

Audubillahi mina Shaytan regime Bismillahu Rahmanur Rahim Allahumma saliya ala Sayyidina Muhammadin Wa ala Ali Sayyidina Muhammadin kamasalayta wa salamta wa barakta wa rahimta wa tarahamta ala Ibrahim Wa ala Ali Ibrahim fil alamina Inna Kahmidu Majid Rabbish Rahli Sadri wa yaserli Amri Wahlul Uqtata millisani of Kahukawli Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu Now that we understand these meanings of Rab and Rahman and Raheem, now that we understand these terms, I want to share with you a beautiful spiritual representation that Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala has created for us through the example of the womb, the Rahem. To quickly reiterate these terms, Rab is a combination of six things in classical Arabic. The definition is a Rabbuhu al-Maliku was Sayyidu al-Murabbi al-Murshid wal-Muna'im al-Qayyim So a Rab is an owner and he is the one with complete authority over its property He is the one who nurtures his creation guides it benefits it by bestowing generous and undeserving gifts upon it and he is the one who maintains it So this is who Allah is, right? That's His primary role with His creation of Rabb. And all His other attributes, they basically center around and they stem from His Rabul biyya. So if someone asks, who is Allah? The answer to that question is Allah is Rabb. Now, as for His nature, His nature is Ar-Rahman and Ar-Raheem. So the manner in which he executes or the way he carries out the functions of his Rubul biyya, it is through intense and consistent love, compassion and mercy.

So now that we understand these concepts, I want to share this example that Allah has created for us through the womb. You know, by studying the womb, we can actually understand a lot about our master's plan for us. Just by studying the relationship of the womb with its fetus. Because this womb, it is the first rub of the fetus. And it demonstrates the exact same principles of Rahmaniyya and Rahimiyya in its interaction with it. This is why there is a Hadith in which Rasulullah , he said This world is a womb for the afterlife. In other words, the story of our lives in this world, it tells a tale about the kind of life that we're going to have in the afterlife because This world, this dunya that we're living in is the womb or access the womb and we are the fetus in that womb. And just as the brief and temporary residence in a womb is actually preparation for this worldly life, Our stay in this temporal world is nothing more than a short duration of preparation for the afterlife. Now, if you look at the Rahem, the womb, you'll see all six principles of Rubbiya at work. It has ownership and it has authority over the embryo, right?

It nurtures the embryo, it helps the embryo grow and develop into a fetus. So the womb is Malik, it is Sayyid and it is Murabbi. Then we see that the womb, it bestows these priceless gifts upon the fetus to the development of its eyes, its nose, its ears, hands, feet, the heart, the intellect and all of its internal and external organs. So we can see that the womb is also the Muna'im, the bestower of gifts. We also know that the womb, it manages the entire development process of the embryo from its conception all the way until it is fully developed. So the womb is also ayam. So we can see that the womb, it actually acts as the very first physical rub that we come in contact with. And this very first act, it actually demonstrates the design of how Allah created this mechanism. It demonstrates the act of Rububiyya by carrying out all six functions of the definition of the word Rab, right? Malik, Sayyid, Murabbi, Murshid, Munhayim, Qayyim. Now, what happens once the baby is delivered into this world?

Who is the baby handed over to? It is handed over to its loving mother who becomes the next immediate Rabb of that baby. Not the father, the mother. It's the mother that becomes the next Rabb. Why? Because she feeds it. She takes care of it. There is this transference of Rubbiya that takes place. The mother now takes ownership of the baby. The mother now takes authority over it. The mother assumes the responsibility of nurturing it, helping it grow and develop, teaching it, guiding it, setting it to purpose, showering all these gifts and blessings upon it. She becomes the one who maintains that baby's sustenance in all its various forms, physical, emotional, psychological.

So we can see that our mothers become the next immediate Arab Right after the Rububiya of the womb, the Raham, it's completed. Now father is also a Rab, but his Rububiya gets executed through the mother. You see, the father always uses the mother as a means for her. He facilitates her functions of Rububiya. That's the role of the father, but the primary caretaker of the child is always the mother. So now let's study this Hadith to better understand the underlying principles that are at work. So Rasulullah , he said, . This temporal world is the womb of the afterlife. So let's examine the fetus and the womb of its mother. Is it the womb actually doing all the work? Or is it the mother doing all the work behind the scenes and letting this womb act as an intermediary between herself and her child?

Is it the womb or the mother? We know it's always the mother, right? The mother is the one taking care of the baby's needs. She is the one eating all the right things. She is making sure she doesn't bump into things so that her baby doesn't get hurt. She's the one getting all the ultrasounds done, taking all those painful but necessary blood tests, all those injections. So she is the one actually suffering for the baby. Baby is living comfortably in the womb, but it's the mother doing all the work, right? The mother is the one doing all the hard work all along. But from the perspective of the fetus, who is doing all the work? The womb, not the mother. You see, the fetus has absolutely no knowledge of its mother.

All it knows, all it recognizes, all it understands is the womb. If I ask the fetus, who do you think is feeding you? Who do you think is nurturing you, taking care of you, sustaining you? Who is doing all the work that is necessary for your health and development? What will the fetus reply? The womb. The fetus has absolutely no knowledge of the existence of its mother. You see? What mother? Where's the mother? I don't see a mother. All I see is the womb.

There is no mother. It's just cause and effect. When I tell this fetus, no, no, it's not the womb, it's the mother. She is the one feeding you. She's the one taking care of you. This womb is only an intermediary. It's a means. And the fetus says, you know, what are you talking about? It's the umbilical cord that's feeding me. That's what gets me this blood that is carrying all the nutrients. I get fed by that, the umbilical cord. The umbilical cord is responsible for my development.

There is no mother. And so I explain, no, no, there is a mother. She is all around you. You are within the love, the care, the concern, and the mercy of your mother. This womb wouldn't exist if she didn't exist. And this womb that you're in, it's actually temporary. This is not the world you were created for. Believe me, this world is filthy, it is dark, it is immensely constricted. There is an amazing and a beautiful world that exists outside this womb that has been created just for you. And that world is so magnificent that you cannot even imagine its glory right now within this womb. Trust me, this womb is filth compared to that world. So if you think this womb is kind and merciful to you, let me tell you, it doesn't even compare to the love and the mercy of your mother.

Because your mother is going to take care of you in the next world. She will shower you with so much love that you have absolutely no idea. You cannot even imagine that while you're in this womb. But the fetus says, what are you talking about? I am really really happy here. Everything I need is being taken care of for me right here. Why do I need to have another world? I don't know why you keep talking to me about this mother and another world and an afterlife. There is no mother. There is no world outside this womb. You're crazy. Okay show me.

Show me this world that you keep talking about. Show it to me right now. I want to see it. Prove to me that there is another world. Prove to me that there is actually a mother. I'm not gonna believe you unless and until I see that world and until I see that mother. And I say, I can't show it to you right now, but I promise when you transition out of this world, this womb, you'll see both of them. Oh, so now I'm supposed to trust you. I'm supposed to trust your belief system, your intellect? What if you're wrong? Now this is us with Allah in this world. There are so many of us denying the existence of the mother living in the comforts of this womb, of this dunya.

So now, I begin this logical path of explanation and I say, look, you have been given these eyes, but there is so little to see here. You've been given these ears, but there's so little to hear. You've been given taste buds, but there is so little to taste here. You have a nose with this magnificent ability to smell, but there's not a single fragrance here. You have arms, you have feet, you have all these amazing gifts, but you cannot benefit from them within this womb. So think about it. These are of no use to you inside this womb, which means there must be another world that is out there, a world where you will be able to use and benefit from these gifts. Think about it. Your only purpose in this womb, in this world, is to draw your sustenance from your mother and develop these organs. In other words, you're here so that you can prepare them for the next world where you will actually be using them, where you will actually benefit from them. But does the fetus understand that?

No. It doesn't. To the fetus, the concept of another world and the existence of a mother is just ridiculous. Just as the concept of a God and an afterlife is absurd to so many of us. So now what happens? This fetus continues to live in its ignorance and its arrogance until the nine months complete. Now what happens? Contractions begin. The fetus starts panicking. What's going on here? What's happening? This is what was promised to you.

I told you this day would come. I told you this world is temporary. So now with those contractions, this beautiful world of the fetus, this magnificent world it was living happily and comfortably in, it starts crumbling around it. It starts falling apart all around it. Now, isn't that exactly the description of the Day of Judgment? When the earth is shaken up with its earthquakes. And the earth discharges its burden. And man says, What is wrong with this world? What is wrong with this earth? Yaw ma izin tuhaddisu akhbaraha bi anna rabbaka o haalaha On this day, it will report the news of which your master has commanded it. Yauma izin, yasduru naasu ashtatan liyurao a'malahum.

On this day, people will separate out, and they will be shown the results of their deeds. Fa man yaamal misqala zarratin khairan yara. So, whoever did an atom's weight of good will see it. Wa man yaamal misqala zarratin sharran yara. and whoever did an Adam's weight of evil will see it so the world of the fetus now comes to an end and it is forced out of it it is pushed out of it against its will you see does the fetus have a choice in whether it wants to stay in the womb or not no whether it wants to or not whether it's ready or not once its time is up that's it It is pushed out into the next world. It dies in the womb in order to be born again in the next world, you see. Its death in the womb results in its creation in this world. That's what the word intaqal means. It comes from naqala, which means a transference. It also means a copy or a replica. That's what naqala means, a copy or a replica.

Why? Because the next world is going to be a copy, it is going to be a replica of the first. If you did good in the world, in this world, you will find good in the next world. If you did evil in this world, you will find evil in the next world. It's going to be a replica, it's going to be a copy. If the fetus has not properly developed its eyes, its ears, its brain, its limbs in the womb of its mother, it is going to suffer the consequences of that in the afterlife of this dunya. SubhanAllah. So now this temporal world of the fetus is destroyed and it comes into this huge world that he was informed about. this world that was promised to him in the womb. He is now forced into this world, this afterlife that he chose not to believe in. And then, as soon as it's out of the womb, who is the baby handed to? The mother.

Subhanallah. The mother that he said did not exist, the mother he denied his entire life in the womb. So you can see that the fetus goes through the exact same confusion of the seen and the unseen while it's in the womb of its mother. That's so many of us go through in this life. The fetus that accepts the rububiya of its mother through the womb comes out fully developed and is now capable of enjoying all the benefits that the afterlife has to offer, which is this physical world for the fetus. But the fetus that rejected the rububia of the womb, it comes out underdeveloped, blind, deaf, mute, physically challenged, mentally challenged, incapable of benefiting from the joys and pleasures that this world has to offer. We are all going through this exact same process in life. Why? Because Ad-Dunya Rahmul Akhra this world is the womb for the afterlife. And here we have our Rab telling us, look, follow the Sharia, keep yourself clean, keep yourself pure, do your Salat, complete your fast, pay your Zakat, fulfill your obligations of Hajj. And what do we say?

Why? How is this going to help me? It's not going to help you here. That's not the purpose. The obligations of Sharia is not meant for this world. It's the sustenance for the development of our spiritual limbs. That's what Sharia is. It's a means like the womb. It's a tool. It's a mechanism, a means, an intermediary for the development of our spiritual limbs, for the development of our spiritual organs that are going to help us live a good life After this world is over, that is where we will benefit from these fully developed spiritual organs. In the afterlife, all we're doing here in this Dunya is developing them in order to use them in the next world, which is Jannah.

But how do you develop them? Through the Shariah. Because Jannah is described as a world that is incredibly beautiful, a world that is governed by a Rab. who is intensely merciful, who is constantly merciful. The Sharia is the umbilical cord providing the sustenance for the development of our spiritual existence, of our spiritual being. Now whether we believe in it or not, whether we want to or not, whether we execute it or not, that next world is inevitable. It's coming. Right? Al Jannatahaqun, Wannarahaqun, Wal Mautahaqun, Wal Barasahaqun, Wal Mizanahaqun, Wa Saratahaqun. Paradise is a reality. Hellfire is a reality. Death is a reality.

Rising from graves is a reality. The scales in which our actions will be weighed, that is a reality. The straight path is a reality. Wa annasaata atiyatun laraibafiha. And that appointed moment, it is coming. There is absolutely no doubt about it. That is the world in which justice will be exacted. Every incident for which you said, where is justice? On that day we will see justice. The innocent people that suffered momentarily in this short span of life, this dunya, this world, their momentary suffering will be balanced out with never-ending gifts and pleasures in the afterlife and the one who caused those sufferings for fleeting gains and pleasures their pleasures will be counterbalanced with grievous pain and everlasting torment but that day of judgment is coming these are all descriptions of the day of judgment when this universe will be destroyed this this world that we are so comfortable in it's going to end that day is coming when souls will be paired together when you will finally meet those loved ones

who left you behind in this world and when that little girl who was buried alive will be asked for what sin were you killed this is the day where Allah will exact justice this is the day of justice not this world not this dunya that we're living in that day all the deeds will open up And when the book of deeds will be made public, wa iza samaa ukushitaat And when the sky will be stripped away, wa izal jaheem usoa'irat And when that hellfire is set ablaze, wa izal jannatu uslifaat And when the paradise is brought near, alimat nafsun ma ahdarat Every soul will know what it has brought with it. All good will be rewarded on that day and all bad will be punished on that day. Allahu Akbar. And the fact of the matter is that we have such a benevolent, such a merciful, such a loving master who is just dying to reward us for the smallest good deed that we do in this world. You know, it has been narrated by the Prophet that there will be a man on the day of judgment and all this man ever did was lend money to others. He was a money lender. And usually such people are black hearted people because of interest and they use that as a mechanism to gain worldly profit. But when this man sent out his servants to collect the money that people owed him, if the person was having a hard time returning back that money, If that's what the servant would return and tell him, he would say, forget about it. So on the day of judgment, this man comes before Allah and he does not have any good deeds to his name, except that he used to do that.

And Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, He displays this man to everyone and He says, will I leave him to be more generous than me? Will I leave this man to be more generous than me? SubhanAllah. He used to forgive people. Do you think I am not going to forgive him today? This is the master, the Rabb that we fail in our abudhiya towards. On this day, every single good deed will be balanced with a reward from an immensely beneficent, from an incredibly loving and compassionate master. All our delusions of grandeur in this world, they will be gone. On that day, the muflis and the ghani, the destitute and the affluent, they will be separated. Rasulullah once asked his companions He asked, you know, man al-muflis. Who is the muflis?

Who is the destitute? They said, al-muflisu manla dinaru wala darhamu hindana ya Rasulullah. The destitute is the one who does not have any darham or dinar to his name. And the Prophet said, no. He said, the greatest destitute of my Ummah on the Day of Judgment. the greatest destitute of my Ummah on the Day of Judgment will be the one who comes with all of his prayers and all of his fasting and all of his Zakat wa ya'ti qat shata mahada wa qudifa haada wa akalamalaha haada wa safaqaddam mahada wa daraba haada but in addition to all of these good deeds he cheated this one he lied to this one, he usurped the wealth of this one, he spilled the blood of this one, he struck this one. And so his good deeds will be taken from his account and put into the account of this one and this one and this one. And when his good deeds run out, before justice is fully served the sins and falls of the remaining victims they will be taken from their accounts and added to his accounts and so despite living an entire life full of worship full of prayers full of fasting paying zakat because of his injustices that he committed with other people because of the hurt that he caused to other people in this world. This man will have to give up all his good deeds and he will have to take on all the horrible sins of his victims and he will finally be thrown into Hellfire.

This person, he said, will be the greatest destitute of my Ummah. May Allah protect us all from being among these destitutes on the Day of Judgment. Wahruddawan an alhamdulillahi rabbil alameen wassalatu wassalamu ala rasuli he saidina Muhammadin khatimin nabiin wassaidul Musaleen wala akhi wa wassi alibnabi talib aashrafil wassayeen walil aimatimin zoriatima taibinatahirin wassalam alayhi majmain al-fatah.

allah - being vs attributes.title: Allah - Being vs Attributes
allah - being vs attributes.base:
Our Uzbillahi mina Shaytan regime Bismillahur Rahmanur Rahim Allahumma Salli Allah Sayyidina Muhammadin Waala Ali Sayyidina Muhammadin Kamasallaita wa salam tawa baraktawa rahim tawa tarahamta Allah Ibrahim Waala Ali Ibrahim Falalamina Inna Kahamidum Majid Rabbish Rahli Sadri Wa Yaserly Amri Wahlul Rukhdatam Ilissani Yaf Kahu Kawli Assalam Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatu Now that we understand the linguistic meanings of the basic terms that I've explained so far in these sessions, now it's time to start with the Basmallah, which is actually the first verse of Suratul Fateha, Bismillah Rahman Rahim. So Arabs had this way of shortening these commonly repeated statements. So if they wanted to refer to Bismillah, Rahman or Raheem, they would instead of saying the statement completely, they would just shorten it down to Basmallah. Right? And so for example, La hawla wala kuwata illa billah, they just simply would call it Hauqala. Similarly, they would use Hamdullah for Alhamdulillahi Rabbila Alameen and so on. So The term Basmala, it actually refers to the first verse of Suratul Fatiha which is Bismillahur Rahmanur Raheem. Now, today what I want to focus on is this concept of being and attributes because Allah is a being, He's an entity and then He has all these various attributes and this is quite a complicated topic so you know tried to make it as simple as possible but there are literally books written on this so it's very difficult to condense this this huge topic but if you look at the statement of Bismillahur Rahmanur Rahim from a grammatical point of view you'll see that in the context of mentioning Allah it uses a noun and it uses two adjectives right the word Allah in Bismillah the word Allah is a noun representing an entity a being and then you have two attributes of Rahma ar-Rahman ar-Rahim right these are the adjectives or the attributes describing the nature of Allah

that he is Allah and his nature is Rahman and Raheem. So let's talk about this distinction between Allah's name and his attributes which is essentially the distinction between the concepts of a noun and adjectives if you look at it from a grammatical point of view. Attributes or adjectives are tools that have been provided to us by language in order for us to understand something. In other words, it is through the combination of these two things, noun and adjectives, or name and attributes, that we actually understand an entity, right? So if you want to gain a complete understanding of an entity, you need to understand its attributes. In the Arabic language, this is called dhat and sifat, being and attributes. So for instance, we have a soul and we have a body, which together constitute our zat, our being. But then soul has certain spiritual attributes, right? It can be kind, it can be brave, intelligent, generous, or it can be weak, it can be coward, it can be dumb, right? In the same way, the body has its own set of physical attributes, fat, thin, black, brown, white, tall, short. And once we understand these spiritual and physical attributes that are describing the entity, which is the soul or the body, we essentially come to recognize the nature of that being.

![](images/152/92005ff6-ab51-4acb-a733-01fbbe1e5f0e.jpg)

So the union of the two, they provide the identity and a complete description of that identity, which then enables our intellects to understand the nature of that being. But the thing is attributes cannot exist without the being, right? It is the Zaat that gives existence to the Sifaat. Attributes can only exist after the existence of the being itself. So if there is no Allah, there cannot be a Rahman and Rahim. So that is why the name Allah is greater in its rank than a Rahman or Rahim on the basis of its precedence. So now if we start breaking down the statement of the Basmala, the term Allah points to His Zaat, to His being. You know, He is a deity named Allah. Allah is the title of His essence. As He says in the Quran, Inna ni anallahu la ilaha illa ana. no doubt I am Allah and there is no one worthy of worship and obedience except me now this noun Allah has adjectives which are his 99 sifat his attributes describing the nature of Allah right these are his various manifestations in his interactions with creation so now you have Al-Rahman, Al-Raheem, Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, Al-Mu'min, Al-Mu'min, Al-Aziz, Al-Jabbar, Al-Mutakabbir, Al-Khalik, Al-Bari, Al-Musawwir, Al-Ghaffar, Al-Kahar, Al-Wahab, Al-Fatah, Al-Alim, Al-Kabid, Al-Basit, Al-Kafid, Al-Rafa, Al-Mu'iz, Al-Muzil, Al-Samir, Al-Basir, Al-Hakam, Al-Hakim, Al-Adil, Al-Latif, Al-Halim, Al-Kabir, Al-Azim, Al-Ghafur, Al-Al-Kabir, Al-Hafiz, Al-Hasib, Al-Karim,

Al-Muqeem, Al-Raqib, Al-Jalil, Al-Mujib, Al-Wasir, Al-Wudud, Al-Majid, Al-Ba'ith, Al-Shaheed, Al-Waqil, Al-Kawi, Al-Mateen, Al-Wali, Al-Hamid, Al-Muhsi, Al-Mubdi, Al-Mu'id, Al-Muhhi, Al-Mumi, Al-Hayy, Al-Qayyum. Al-Wajid, Al-Majid, Al-Wahid, Al-Samad, Al-Qadil, Al-Muqtadir, Al-Muqaddim, Al-Mu'akhir, Al-Awal, Al-Akhir, Al-Zahir, Al-Batin, Al-Wali, Al-Muta'ali, Al-Bir, Al-Tawwab, Al-Muntakim, Al-Afoo, Al-Ra'oof. Al-Malik, Al-Mulk, Dhul Jalali, Wali Karam, Al-Muqsit, Al-Jamiya, Al-Ghani, Al-Mukni, Al-Maniya, Adhdar, An-Nafir, An-Noor, Al-Hadi, Al-Badir, Al-Baqi, Al-Warif, Al-Rashid, Al-Sabur, Al-Hanan, Al-Manan, Al-Dayan, Al-Burhan So now these are all these attributes that describe the nature of Allah and to use the example of the prism and the light that I stated in one of the previous sessions Now you can think of Allah as the term Allah as one pure light, right? He is the light of the heavens and the earth. Now when this pure light of the name Allah comes into the physical realm, His divine attributes refract within creation. The light of Allah splits into these 99 attributes within His creation. so now we get all these different manifestations of Allah's essence based on His interaction with His creation so in one instance we see that Allah is Kareem He is generous but then in another instance we see He is Jabbar the compeller in another instance we see He is Ahar the subduer in another we see that He is Al-Aziz the powerful in another we see He is Musil the one who humbles but then he's also al-mua is the one who bestows honor so his essence manifests through all these different attributes within creation this world then becomes a theater for the divine manifestation of Allah's attributes enabling us to know who Allah is not directly through his essence but through the refraction of His attributes and His creations. This is why it is said, La tafakkur fi laa, walaa kin tafakkur fi khal qillah, do not reflect upon Allah, but rather reflect upon the creations of Allah. Why?

Because it is creation, it is nature that manifests all of His attributes for us. So if you want to understand Allah, look outside yourself and look within yourself. We will keep showing them our signs within their own, within the horizons and within their own souls until it becomes perfectly clear to them that all of this is from Alhaq. But then Allah is infinite. and so are his attributes this is why when we attempt to understand Allah we get bewildered by his attributes because in a sense we cannot know what God is any more than we can know what God isn't you see because when we speak about Allah we are speaking about this infinite creator of the heavens and the earth. And the word infinite means without a limit. Now the word in Arabic for definition is the same word that we use for a limitation or a boundary. A definition is what defines or gives finiteness to something, a concept. It limits it, it demarcates it, it puts it into perspective. So when we talk about Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala, we cannot define God. Because to define Him would mean to give Him a hut, a boundary, right?

We would have to place Him in a limit, which is impossible, because, you know, He is without any limit. The way the intellect works, Aqala means to create a boundary. Right? That's the only way human intellect works. That's the only way we know how to grasp or understand something by creating a boundary, by creating a limit. And Allah cannot be limited. And this is why scholars say that all of Aqeedah, this concept of creed, it can be reduced into two statements. He is unlike anything. La yush bihuzatuhu al-zawaat wala muta'atila tus sifaat That His essence is not like any other essence and His attributes are not in any way metaphorical. He is al-ghaniyu anil jameer wal jameeru muftaqarun ilaih He has no need of anyone and everyone is in need of Him. So this statement actually negates need for Allah and it enforces need for the rest of creation. It negates independence for us.

![](images/152/12b65610-07b1-45a5-be3a-0ebb449a5e2f.jpg)

Now here is where we get into another central problem with religion and that is the problem of transcendence and eminence. transcendence is when we speak about God without anything you know any reference in this world that can guide us to him there is nothing in the world for which we can say you know that is God or this is like God because Allah is above and beyond anything they ascribe to so when we talk about transcendence we're talking about Allah being above and beyond everything that we know of right that's why we say subhanaka which is in Arabic the word it means transcendence and it comes from which means to purify to get rid of filth you know to transcend something to be above and beyond something so Allah is transcendent But then pure transcendence has a lot of problems by itself. Because then now Allah becomes the God of the scientist. Like Einstein believed in a God, but he did not believe in a personal God, right? He believed in a transcendent God. The God he believed in was the God of the deist who has nothing to do with his creation. And then that again creates a major problem. But then there is also this concept of eminence, the idea of God being close to us in the world. So for example, like in Hinduism, right, the Brahman class, they don't really believe in idols. You know, we generally, when we think of a Hindu, we think they are idol worshipers, but this class of Brahmans, right, they don't really believe in idols.

It's really a kind of trick to help all these stupid people of the lower class that they believe who they feel that still need to evolve. So there's this understanding in their tradition that the lower classes or the caste system that they have, which they call the varna. So if you're in a lesser varna, you cannot understand the Brahma. That's what they believe because he has gone through several lifetimes to get this ability to perceive. and It is something that only he can perceive and only he can understand the Godhead as they call it Right, so so brahma understands the God that has no attribute Which they call the nirguna but they have this idea that the lower class people actually need to see something in order to understand God and So they gave them all these idols. Aurudubillahi mina Shaytana regime Bismillahur Rahmanur Rahim Allahumma saliya ala saydana Muhammadin wala ali saydana Muhammadin wabariq wa salam Kamasalaytawa salam tawa barak tawa rahim tawa tarahum tawa tawa tawa ali Ibrahim wala ali Ibrahim Fila alamina inna kahamidun majid Rabbish rahli sadri wa yaserli amri wahlul uqdatamil lisani yaf kahu kawli Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu In the last few sessions, we completed our discussion on these first three verses of Surah Al-Fateha Bismillah Rahman Raheem Alhamdulillah Rabil Alameena Rahman Raheem all of which are a testimony to Allah's abundant and consistent love and grace. He is the master of everything that exists in creation and for that he is owed al-hamd which is sincere praise and unconditional gratitude. Today we're going to look at the next verse which is Maliki yawmidin. We'll begin with a linguistic analysis of these three words to get a better understanding of exactly what this means so this verse Maliki yawmidin there are two forms of recitation for this verse there is the Kufi style of recitation which is what we recite generally Maliki yawmidin but there's another school of thought which recites this as Maliki yawmidin and actually both forms are valid so we'll look at both variations the word Malik as we know by now it means an owner right even in Urdu the word Malik means owner and it comes from these three root letters mem, lam and kaf which is milk and the word milk actually means property so the one who owns property is called the Malik of that property right now there's another word in Arabic that shares the same three root letters and that is mulk which means kingdom and the one who rules over a kingdom is called malik king so Allah talks about both in the Quran there is this concept of milqiya and there is mulqiya The word milqiya means ownership and mulqiya means kingship. And Allah ascribes both these attributes to Himself. So He is not only the owner, He is also the king. Because He is the one who judges, the one who decrees, who legislates, who has the ultimate authority over everything in His kingdom.

There is no one above the king that a plaintiff can plead his case with. So, Allah says in Surah Al-Zumar, He says, Wa maqadar Allaha haqqa adrihi wal ardu jami'an qabdatuhu yawmal qiyamati was sama'waatum mutuyyaatum bi yamini subhanahu wa ta'ala amma'isharikoon They did not give Allah a just estimation that was due to Him. And on the day of the resurrection, the entire earth will be grasped by his hand and heavens will be rolled up in his right hand. Now, what does he mean by having it all in his right hand? It basically means it's an ancient Arabic expression that actually means under his complete control, right? This is milqiya, complete ownership. In another verse, he says, Qulillahumma malikal mulk, tu'ti almulkaman tasha wa tunzi almulkamin mantasha wa tuaizu mantasha wa tuzilu mantasha, biyadikal khair inna kaalakuli shayinuqadira. So, this verse begins by saying that Ulillahumma malikal mulk, declare that Allah is the king of all kingdoms. Right? Here he talks about himself as being the king, Malik. So you can see that both forms are used in the Quran. He is Malik and he is Malik.

He is the owner of the day of judgment and he is also the king of the day of judgment. And both these terms have this implication that nobody will be able to question him about any of his decisions and he alone will pass all judgment and make all the final decisions so that is malik or malik the next word is yaum which is actually quite an interesting word in arabic like maliki yaum iddin now generally this statement is translated as a day, right? Yaum is translated as day, owner of the day of judgment. But linguistically, yaum does not actually mean a 24-hour day. What it means is a time interval. It can mean any period of time. So yaum could be used for a moment. It could be used for an hour. It could mean a day, it could mean a month, a year. It could also mean several thousand years.

So, it is simply a duration of time allocated for, you know, a specific purpose. That's what a yawm is. So, for instance, in the Quran, Allah says, ... The angels and the spirit ascend to Him during a Yawm, the extent of which is 50,000 years. So, here Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala specifies Yawm as being equal to 50,000 years. In Surat al-Muzammil, He says, Yawma turjaf al-ardu al-jibalu wakanat al-jibalu kathibam mahila. that moment when the earth and the mountains will convulse and you will see that mountains will turn into a heap of sand that is being poured down. Here, he uses the same word yaum, yaum mater jafu for a moment. So the word yaum can be used for various periods of time, including time itself. So, in Suratul Fateha, he says, Maaliki yawmid deen. Owner of the time period of deen. Right?

So, now let's look at deen. The word deen in the Arabic language comes from the root letters dain, which has several meanings. One of the meanings of dain is, you know, it is a type of rain that falls over and over again until it brings the dead earth back to life. Another meaning of dain is to discipline something. Mandana nafsuhu, whoever disciplines his soul. It also means a way of life. Lakum deenakum waliyadin, you have your way of life and we have ours. Right? But the root meaning of the word 'Dain' actually means debt. Our religion is called Deen-ul-Islam, the Deen of Islam and literally this can be translated as the debt of submission. In other words, the idea is that we have been endowed with innumerable and invaluable blessings by our Master.

And so for all those blessings, we owe our Creator a debt of submission. Allah says, Afa ghaira deen allahi yaboon (Do they seek other than the deen of Allah?) Wa lahu aslamaman fissama waathi wal ardhi tawaan hawqarhan while all creatures in the heaven and the earth have bowed down to Him in submission, willingly or unwillingly. So what Allah is asking here is that do they seek other than repaying this debt when in reality everyone and everything in existence is paying its debt to its creator? They're all in a state of submission, willingly or unwillingly. Now, there are areas of submission that the human being recognizes. One of them is our call to nature. We have to do certain things that we just cannot avoid. And one of them is, for instance, to eat. That is part of our nature. When we get hungry we must eat or we die. We need to drink water when we are thirsty.

If we don't drink, we die. We have to relieve ourselves once we have eaten or taken drink. We don't really have a choice in these matters, do we? We have to do them whether we want to or not. We have to sleep. When sleep comes upon us, we can fight it for a while, but eventually we have to submit or we go into acute psychosis. So there is this idea of willing or unwilling submission to nature itself. But then there is also submission to our own beings, to our own physical bodies. We have limitations. We can eat, but there is only so much that we can eat. We can only drink so much. We can only do so much physical work before we get exhausted.

Right? We have limitations in our movements because of the structure of our bodies. So there is a type of submission of the self. given that we are temporal creatures that are limited by our physical aspects. Now the Arabic word for a boundary or a limit is had. So all of creation have hudud, right? We are all confined within our limits, within our boundaries. We cannot go outside those boundaries. Water cannot flow upwards. A rock cannot fly. A bird cannot bark. A dog cannot sing.

Honey will always stay sweet. Citrus will always stay sour. So in the Quran, there is this idea of limitations that everything is in a state of submission to its limitations. Every creature is confined within its boundaries it's hadud. and they are confined within it willingly or unwillingly. So in other words, they are all in a state of submission. And then Allah follows the statement with a reminder that they will all be returned back to their owner. And to him is their return. Now if you deeply reflect upon creation itself, you'll see that there are things that are emerging and then they are returning back into non-existence. Everything that has life comes into existence and then returns back into non-existence. Plants, vegetables, the animal kingdom and ultimately even the mineral kingdom. they're all returning to non-existence after they came into existence.

So in other words, everything that is in existence is paying back its debt to its creator, except the human beings, you see. It is only human beings who are not actively paying back their debt of submission, their dinul Islam. But the difference here is that We are also not being asked about our debts right now. So when will we be asked? And who will ask us about these debts? Maliki Yawmitti, the owner and the king of that time period when the debt of submission falls due. So Yawm al-Din is that time period when the debt of submission falls due. It's payback time. Qaifamma tu dinu tu dhanu How you transact with others is the way you will be transacted with. This is why this time period is also called Yawm al-Hisab the time of accountability. Rasulullah said in one of his Hadiths , he said, Take yourself to account before you are taken to account.

So there is a debt of submission that we owe Allah . But then there is also a debt that Allah will owe us on that day. You see? When a master issues a command to his slave the fulfillment of that command is a debt that the slave owes to his master because there are only two possibilities he either obeys the command or he disobeys it in both cases a return or a recompense falls due upon the master you see if the slave obeyed his master and executed his command properly, then his master owes him a reward. But if he disobeyed his master's command, the master now owes him punishment. That's Yawmud-Din, that's Yawmud-Hisab, the day when that debt falls due. This is why Allah calls upon people to actually owe him a debt. He says in the Quran, Who will indebt Allah with a beautiful debt? So Allah is asking us for a loan. Who will indebt Allah with a beautiful debt?

Why is Allah asking us for a loan? So that Allah multiplies its rewards many many times over and returns it back to his life. So in this verse, Allah is actually asking His slaves, Who among you will give me a loan? Right? Who among you will indebt me with His willing submission of 'ubu diyya, so that I can multiply its rewards many many times over and pay it back to you. For He has the most noble rewards. Subhanallah. Even on that day of hisaab, this Malik is full of love and mercy. So that is what Malik-i-Aumiddin linguistically means. The king or the owner of the time period when the debt of submission falls due. Now let's look at some of the implications of this verse. The most important aspect of this verse is that it addresses this notion of an unjust world.

We know so many people today have given up faith and this belief in the existence of a creator based on the injustices that they see in this world, right? They look at all of this injustice that goes on around in this world and they use that as proof against God. Now this can be based on an injustice that happened to them personally or injustices that happens to another. And their argument is that if there is a God that is so loving and caring, then how come He let all of this happen? Now, what's interesting about that, especially to us as a Muslim, is that nowhere in the Quran, Allah claims or promises to give us a good life in this world. Nowhere. In fact, what He promises every human being is quite the opposite. He says, in Surat-ul-Baqarah, He says, wala nabluwannakum bishayim minal khawfi wal jewari wa naqsim minal amwali wal anfusi wa thamaraat. And no doubt about it, indeed, surely we shall test you with fear. with hunger, with loss of wealth, with loss of life, children, with loss of crops. But then he says, O Bashir Sabireen and for the patient ones there are glad tidings. In Surah Al-Mulk, he says, Tabaaraka ladi biyadi hil mulk wa hua'ala kuli shayinu qadeer Blessed is the one whose hand has the ultimate dominion and is able to do everything.

Alladi khalaqal mawta wal hayata liyabluwaqum ayyukum ahsanu 'Amala Who created death and life to test you and see which of you is the best in action. according to the Quran this world was never meant for justice according to the Quran this life is a test and this world that we live in is an examination hall and everyone is being tested some with poverty some with wealth some with sickness some with health in fact the healthy and the rich are going through a much more difficult test than the sick and the poor. Because they will be held accountable for these gifts. You know, I gave you all this, show me what you did with it.
