worship and assistance.title: Worship and Assistance
worship and assistance.base:
Ahudubillahiminas Shaytana regime Bismillahir Rahmanir Rahim Allahumma salli Allah saydana Muhammadin Wa ala ali saydana Muhammadin Kamasallaita wa salamta wa baraktawa rahimtawa tarahamta ala Ibrahim wa ala ali Ibrahim fil alamina inna Kahamidun Majid Rabbish Rahli Sadri Wa yasserli Amri Wahlul Uqdatamillisani of Kahukawli Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatu We completed the linguistic study of the first four verses of Surah Al-Fateha. So now we have, after giving us an introduction of who Allah is through the first, or rather the beginning verses, then he says, Iya kana abudu wa iya kana sta'in. It is only you that we worship or willingly enslave ourselves to. And it is only you that we seek help from. Now here, there's something really interesting in this verse. If you notice, there is a complete change of tone over here. So the previous verses, they were all in the third person, right? They were informational. So bismillah rahman rahim. begin with the name of Allah extremely merciful intensely merciful all praise and glory belongs to Allah who is the master of all universes or everything that is known the abundant the abundantly merciful the consistently merciful owner of a time when the dead of submission falls due so these are all statements if you notice they're all in the third person in which Allah is just basically informing us about who He is.

But then, He suddenly changes the tone and He turns it into a second person conversation. He turns it into a dua, as if we are now speaking directly with Him. it is only you we worship and it is only you we turn to for help the tone of this verse is not that Allah is the one that we worship and Allah is the one that we turn to help it's not in the third person it's as if we are in direct conversation with Allah at this point and this is a beautiful linguistic tool in the Arabic language that is called Il-Tifaat which is a sudden change in the pronoun of the speaker, or the one that is being spoken to. So Allah constantly changes the conversation in the Quran from third person to first person, then to second person, and then back to third person, right? And you can see this in almost every single surah. He sometimes refers to Himself using I, sometimes He uses we, right? Sometimes he uses him. These are all linguistic tools to not only keep the reader alert and awake, but also a mechanism to highlight what Allah wants from us. So in the case of Surah Al-Fateha, you can see that the tone now suddenly changes to a du'a, it changes to a supplication. It is only you we worship and it is only you we turn to for help.

And who is the one saying that? It is you and I that are saying that. So we are now in direct conversation with Allah. And this style of switching suddenly from third person to second person is a means of letting us know that this is in fact what Allah wants from us. You understand? When we say ... because this is all revelation coming from Allah, right? We are not the authors of Quran. So this is all revelation coming from Allah. So now imagine a book like Quran, something so meaningful. How is Allah to have this conversation with us where suddenly now He wants us, while He's describing Himself, He wants us to know what He wants from us. So by changing his tone to Iya kanabudu wa ya kanasta'in, Allah is expressing His intention of wanting us to say that we willingly worship you and we freely give up our freedom and desires to become your slaves.

In other words, Allah is not commanding us into slavery by saying Istaabadu anfusikum li Enslave yourselves to Me. Instead, He wants us to say Iya kanabudu It is only you that we want to worship. In other words, Allah is asking us to reach this conclusion of our wudiya on our own, through the study of the previous three verses. The idea is that when we truly understand the meaning of Alhamdulillahi Rabbil Alameen, when we truly understand the meaning of Ar-Rahmanir Raheem and when we truly understand the meaning of Maliki Yawmid Deen, And when we recognize what an incredibly loving, merciful, and powerful Rabb Allah is, our natural and logical conclusion to that understanding has to be . You see? Our natural response has to be a willing desire of submission. So the idea here is that if you haven't reached that conclusion all by yourself, then don't say it. Now let's look at this verse linguistically. The first word is iyaqa, which means only you. So, linguistically, iyaka excludes everything and everyone except the object of the conversation. The next word is... naabudu which means we worship and naabudu comes from the word ibada which we all know means worship which in turn comes from the root word abd which means slave now what is the connection between worship and slavery what's the relationship there the relationship is that worship is a demonstration of one's slavery Worship or Aibada is a demonstration of one's acceptance of slavery. So we say iya ka nabudu, it is you that we worship. And the next thing we say is iya ka nastain, it is only you that we seek assistance from. Now the word nastain, it comes from istaana, which in turn then comes from the root word aun, and it means assistance. Now, there are many other words in Arabic for help, right?
